rationale: D gives the most economical complete argument: it chooses constants in dependency order and integrates the uniform common-incidence bound directly to obtain the contradiction. A supplies an excellent overview and particularly precise slicing-kernel and singular-value estimates, though with more scaffolding. B also completes the argument and explains the exceptional-set estimates well, but adds normalization bookkeeping and describes the singular-value/wedge relationship less precisely than A. C has a sound underlying argument but cites two equations absent from the supplied context; their elementary derivations can be reconstructed, yet these omissions and the weaker sectioning make verification less convenient.
